capabilities.test_contract: Launch the CLI mcp-server entry with a scoped env; assert tools callable; negative: with OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES=true and empty OMNIROUTE_MCP_SCOPES, tool calls are rejected as missing_scopes.

capabilities.purpose: evaluateToolScopes checks each tool's required scopes from MCP_TOOL_MAP against caller scopes resolved authInfo→meta→env, with wildcard support and fail-closed tool_definition_missing; enforcement runs only when OMNIROUTE_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES==='true' (server.ts:104) — otherwise every caller is allowed (scopeEnforcement.ts:107-109); resolveMcpCallerAuthInfo binds real per-key api_keys.scopes on HTTP/SSE and fails closed to the fallback chain. capabilities.purpose: GET routes expose the MCP tool catalog and runtime status to management callers, accepting the mcp:connect scope; read-only introspection used by the dashboard Endpoints page. capabilities.name: A2A JSON-RPC endpoint (/a2a)
capabilities.purpose: The /a2a router serves A2A v0.3 methods (message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/cancel) plus v1.0 aliases (SendMessage/SendStreamingMessage, route.ts:31-34), and rejectIfA2ADisabled returns JSON-RPC -32000/503 unless settings.a2aEnabled===true (default false, settings.ts:173). Collision: this endpoint lets OmniRoute act as an agent peer accepting task delegation from foreign agents — the exact inverse of KK3's sole-orchestrator rule, hence disabled by default and owner-gated.
capabilities.risk_class: high — inbound task delegation channel from arbitrary A2A clients when enabled
capabilities.test_contract: Enable in lab, run message/send against a builtin skill and a v1.0 alias; negative: disabled state returns error code -32000 with HTTP 503.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: settings.a2aEnabled=false (default) — every method short-circuits at rejectIfA2ADisabled.

capabilities.name: A2A task manager (lifecycle state machine)
capabilities.purpose: A2ATaskManager runs submitted→working→completed|failed|cancelled transitions with UUID ids, in-memory storage with optional SQLite persistence, 5-minute default TTL, a concurrent-task limit, and GHSA-jcm5 owner scoping (sha256 of the API key; ownerless keyless tasks stay visible to every caller by design, taskManager.ts:49-54). Collision: durable task state inside the gateway is orchestration state — if A2A is ever enabled, KK3 must treat this store as subordinate state, never truth.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — in-memory task state with a keyless-visible ownership carve-out
capabilities.test_contract: Drive a task through every legal transition; negative: illegal transition rejected; persistence: enable SQLite backing and restart to confirm reload.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Only reachable when a2aEnabled; clearing in-memory state is process restart; TTL expiry reaps stale tasks.

capabilities.name: A2A authentication posture (keyless local-first)
capabilities.purpose: authenticateA2ARequest mirrors the /v1 posture: REQUIRE_API_KEY on → valid OmniRoute key required; else OMNIROUTE_API_KEY env → timing-safe token match; else keyless allow (authenticate.ts:40-41), with resolveA2AOwner hashing the key for task scoping; the REST task routes independently re-check a2aEnabled!==true (tasks/route.ts:119). Collision: under the local-first keyless default any LAN peer could drive agent tasks the moment the feature flag flips — the flag and the key posture are separate axes the owner must set together.

capabilities.test_contract: With A2A enabled: no key → 401 when REQUIRE_API_KEY=true; wrong key rejected via timing-safe compare; keyless mode allowed and ownerless tasks listed.

capabilities.name: A2A agent card discovery (/.well-known/agent.json)

Collision: the card advertises OmniRoute-as-agent to any discovering orchestrator — marketing the control plane KK3 does not want advertised; centrally MANAGEMENT-classified (non-/api path falls to the fail-closed default).
capabilities.risk_class: low — read-only advertisement, but it publishes capability metadata (and a stale version fallback) to any authenticated peer
capabilities.test_contract: GET the well-known route and the agent-card.json twin; assert the card validates; content check: version matches package.json when run under npm.

capabilities.name: A2A built-in agent skills (6 handlers)
capabilities.purpose: A2A_SKILL_HANDLERS lazily imports six builtin skills (smart-routing, quota-management, provider-discovery, cost-analysis, health-report, list-capabilities) that execute prompts through the OmniRoute pipeline and return routing_explanation/cost/resilience/policy metadata. capabilities.name: ACP CLI-agent registry (host CLI detection)
capabilities.purpose: detectInstalledAgents probes the host for codex/claude/gemini/goose (+operator-defined custom) agent CLIs by execFileSync'ing their version commands (registry.ts:13, definitions at :53); POST accepts client-chosen custom binaries persisted to settings; the routeGuard comments classify /api/acp/agents as an RCE-via-tunnel spawn surface and gate it LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:72). Collision: the registry exists so OmniRoute can discover and drive host agent CLIs — an orchestration-adjacent capability that steps on KK3's commissioning authority; the LOCAL_ONLY tier is the quarantine.
capabilities.risk_class: high — version-probe spawns plus client-defined binary registration (loopback-constrained)
capabilities.test_contract: GET the route from loopback and assert detection shape; negative: non-loopback peer denied by the LOCAL_ONLY tier; register a custom agent then remove it.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier blocks remote callers; deleting settings.customAgents removes custom entries; no global enable flag exists because detection is on-demand only.

capabilities.name: ACP process spawner (CLI-as-backend transport)
capabilities.purpose: AcpManager.spawn launches a registered CLI agent as a child process with piped stdio, shell:false, and the FULL OmniRoute process env merged under caller-supplied env (manager.ts:65-69) — Coder-X corroborated the unfiltered env inheritance: provider credentials present in the gateway env flow into agent children; hasRegisteredAgent is the only quarantine (:54), and no production call site outside src/lib/acp references AcpManager (grep-verified — currently unwired). Collision: OmniRoute spawning agent processes is precisely the process-spawning class the HX disabled-by-default rule freezes, and 'CLI-as-backend' makes the gateway an agent runtime competing with KK3's execution substrate.
capabilities.risk_class: critical — child processes inherit gateway env secrets; arbitrary registered binaries
capabilities.test_contract: Static: assert no route wiring reaches spawn (grep); dynamic lab: register a benign CLI, spawn, assert env allowlisting requirement before any HX use.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: No runtime wiring exists today (inert); if ever wired, the registry whitelist plus the LOCAL_ONLY API tier are the quarantine; removing custom agents closes the binary set.

capabilities.name: Memory engine (per-key long-term memory store)
capabilities.purpose: The memory engine provides CRUD over typed memory rows (api-key-scoped, session-optional, TTL/expiry, TV6 typed-decay columns) with a 60s/500-entry cache; getMemorySettings defaults enabled:false (settings.ts:33,101) and the REST API is management-gated. Collision: a second long-term memory living inside the traffic gateway competes with Carol's catalog/second-brain governance (who owns remembered knowledge, provenance, expiry) — the HX lane keeps it disabled by default.
capabilities.risk_class: high — persistent per-key memory that silently shapes future prompts if enabled
capabilities.test_contract: Disabled: retrieve returns empty and injection is skipped; enabled lab: create/retrieve/expire a memory and assert api-key scoping isolation between two keys.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: memoryEnabled=false (default) disables retrieval, injection, and the reindex path; rows persist but stay unread — delete via the management API for full quarantine.

capabilities.name: Memory+skills injection into the chat traffic path
capabilities.purpose: injectMemoryAndSkills runs on every chat request: it retrieves owner memories (memorySkillsInjection.ts:116) and injects them plus enabled skill tools into the outbound body; the per-request x-omniroute-no-memory:true header nulls the owner and disables both branches (chatCore.ts:1248-1252). Collision: silent prompt mutation inside the traffic plane — invisible to clients unless they send the opt-out header — is an observability and owner-authority concern even when memory itself is approved.
capabilities.risk_class: high — in-path request mutation; default-on once memoryEnabled
capabilities.test_contract: With memory enabled, assert an injected block appears and that the opt-out header removes it; negative: memoryEnabled=false injects nothing.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: memoryEnabled=false globally; per-request x-omniroute-no-memory:true header (always available).

capabilities.name: Memory vector backends (sqlite / Qdrant / Obsidian)
capabilities.purpose: Memory backends are pluggable behind the MemoryBackend interface: local SQLite vectors (default), an external Qdrant cluster (host/port/apiKey/collection/quantization config, qdrant.ts:16-26), and an Obsidian backend that reads/writes memories as Markdown+frontmatter files in a user vault path (obsidianBackend.ts:2-29). Collision: Qdrant moves governed memory content to an external service (egress + retention outside the plane) and Obsidian writes into arbitrary user filesystem locations — both need an owner decision on data placement; backend selection lives in memory settings and all backends die with memoryEnabled=false.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — external/filesystem data placement of memory content
capabilities.test_contract: Lab: point at a throwaway Qdrant collection and a temp vault dir, assert round-trip; negative: unreachable Qdrant degrades per backend health check.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Backend selection reverts to sqlite; memoryEnabled=false disables all backends; no external target is contacted while disabled.

capabilities.name: Embeddings backing service (memory + /v1/embeddings)
capabilities.purpose: createEmbeddingResponse routes embedding requests through the provider/combo machinery (embeddingRegistry, familyGuard dimension checks) and treats private/LAN hosts as trusted no-auth per the #6925 comment (service.ts:39-40) with outbound URL guard imports for cloud targets. Collision: minor — it is traffic-plane, but it is also the memory pipeline's embedding source, so memory enablement inherits its LAN trust posture; no orchestration content.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — LAN no-auth trust class for the embeddings route feeds the memory pipeline
dependencies: provider or combo with an embedding model
capabilities.test_contract: Direct: POST /v1/embeddings against a configured provider; negative: unknown embedding provider yields the formatted error; persistence: none.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Traffic-plane standard path; removing embedding providers/combos disables it; memoryEnabled=false removes the memory consumer.

capabilities.name: Skill registry + executor
capabilities.purpose: SkillExecutor.execute blocks only when settings.skillsEnabled === false (executor.ts:43-46) — getSettings carries NO hardcoded skillsEnabled default (grep-verified across src/lib/db), so an unpersisted key means execution is allowed; executions are audited into skill_executions rows (:64-75) and skills are stored per api-key with enabled/mode flags (registry.ts:119-130). Collision: user-defined executable capabilities inside the gateway bypass KK3's work-order scoping, and the default-allow gate means the disabled-by-default rule is NOT enforced by the code for this surface — an owner-set skillsEnabled=false row is required to actually disable it.
capabilities.risk_class: high — default-allow execution gate contradicts the HX disabled-by-default rule until explicitly set
capabilities.test_contract: Unset key: execute a builtin skill via /api/skills/executions and record that it runs (evidence of default-allow); set skillsEnabled=false and assert the 403-style error; per-skill enabled=false rejects by name.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Persist settings.skillsEnabled=false (explicit — the code default is allow); per-skill enabled=false in the registry; management API is requireManagementAuth-gated.

capabilities.name: Skill tool injection + interception in provider requests
capabilities.purpose: Enabled skills are advertised to models as provider-native tools (name@version, base64url-encoded under the omr_skill_ prefix when needed, injection.ts:33-41) and their calls are intercepted and executed gateway-side with builtin aliasing (web_search/web_fetch fallbacks, interception.ts:31-34); customSkillExecutionEnabled===false blocks custom-skill interception (:279). Collision: this gives models tool-level access to gateway-managed capabilities — agent-like autonomous behavior inside the traffic plane, gated only by the same default-allow skills posture (CAP-P7-018).
capabilities.risk_class: high — models gain executable tools mid-stream
capabilities.test_contract: With a test skill enabled, assert the tool appears in the outbound payload and its call is intercepted; negative: skillsEnabled=false strips injection (memorySkillsInjection both-branch disable).
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: skillsEnabled=false globally; per-skill enabled=false; builtinToolNames allowlist constrains builtins per request.

capabilities.name: Skill sandbox (container-runtime execution)
capabilities.purpose: SandboxRunner executes skill code in containers (docker/apple/wsl/orbstack/podman auto-detected, SKILLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME override, containerProvider.ts:12-15) with defaults cpu 100 / mem 256MB / 30s timeout / network disabled / read-only fs (sandbox.ts:25-31); runtime detection probes binaries via spawnSync and fails closed when none exists (containerProvider.ts:71-79). Collision: container spawning on the host is the process-spawning class — on HX hosts container runtimes are rick's plane, so this stays lab-only; the isolation defaults are sound but the capability itself needs an owner decision.
capabilities.risk_class: high — host container execution; mitigated by network-off/read-only defaults and fail-closed runtime detection
dependencies: a container runtime on the host
capabilities.test_contract: Lab only: run a trivial image and assert network-isolation and read-only flags reach the runtime command; negative: no runtime installed → provider resolution fails, no spawn.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: No container runtime on the host → hard fail-closed; SKILLS_SANDBOX_RUNTIME can pin or the sandbox caller path stays unused while skills are disabled.

capabilities.name: Built-in + memory-builtin skill handlers
capabilities.purpose: builtinSkills and memoryBuiltinHandlers provide the prepackaged handlers (web_search, web_fetch with pinned fetch-backend support, browser, and memory CRUD tools surfaced as model-callable tools, MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES at interception.ts:36) registered at startup with a chunk-singleton fallback. Collision: memory builtins give models direct write access to the memory store when memory is enabled — model-driven memory mutation crosses into Carol's knowledge-governance lane; otherwise standard capability code.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — model-invokable memory mutation among otherwise benign builtins
capabilities.test_contract: Execute each builtin directly with a test input; negative: builtin not in the request allowlist is not resolved (interception.ts:44-49).
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Same gates as CAP-P7-018/019; memory builtins additionally die with memoryEnabled=false.

capabilities.name: skills.sh external skill provider install
capabilities.purpose: The skillssh install route fetches third-party SKILL.md content via fetchSkillMd and registers it globally, but only when the active skills provider setting is 'skillssh' (409 otherwise, route.ts:23-32); authenticated via isAuthenticated. Collision: importing unvetted external skill definitions is a supply-chain path into the skill registry (and from there into model tool lists) — owner approval and content provenance review belong before any use.
capabilities.risk_class: high — third-party content supply chain into executable skills
capabilities.test_contract: With provider=skillssh, install a known test skill and assert registry row + provenance fields; negative: provider unset returns 409.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Provider setting not switched (default path rejects with 409); uninstall removes the registry row.

capabilities.name: GitHub skill collector (external repo discovery + install)
capabilities.purpose: githubCollector searches GitHub for SKILL.md-bearing repos, scores them, scans for blocked patterns (malware/secrets), and installs skill files INTO EXTERNAL AGENT DIRECTORIES (Hermes, Claude, etc. per the module header, githubCollector.ts:1-11). Collision: it reaches out to GitHub (egress) and writes into other agents' host directories — crossing the owner authority plane and other lanes' filesystems; the blocked-pattern scan is the only quarantine besides not calling it.
capabilities.risk_class: high — writes to foreign agent directories plus GitHub egress
dependencies: target agent directories on the host
capabilities.test_contract: Dry-run a search and inspect scoring; negative: a repo matching blocked patterns is refused; never run install outside a lab directory.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: On-demand API only (no scheduler found); skipping use leaves nothing running; installed files are plain files removable by hand.

capabilities.name: Skill Collector CLI detection + chaos dispatch
capabilities.purpose: The /api/skills/collect/ tree probes the host for installed CLI tools via child-process detection — classified RCE-via-tunnel and gated LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:69) — while the single chaos dispatch route is PUBLIC-by-exact-path but enforces its own Bearer validateApiKey check (chaos/route.ts:67) per the publicApiRoutes.ts:54-60 contract. Collision: host probing plus an externally-triggerable dispatch endpoint into skill execution — the LOCAL_ONLY tier covers the probes; chaos mode is the one intentionally-public hole and needs its flag+key evidence before any owner sign-off.
capabilities.risk_class: high — host CLI probing; one public exact route with per-handler auth
dependencies: chaos mode flag for the chaos route
capabilities.test_contract: GET detect from loopback (shape check) and from LAN (expect LOCAL_ONLY denial); POST chaos without a key (expect 401) and with a key when enabled.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: LOCAL_ONLY tier for /api/skills/collect/; chaos requires its own enabled flag plus a valid key — both absent by default.

capabilities.name: Agent-skills catalog + skills/ SKILL.md corpus
capabilities.purpose: 45 generated SKILL.md manifests (23 API + CLI families per skills/README.md and the generator header 'all 45 agent skills', generator.ts:2) teach any external agent (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, Cline, Continue) how to drive OmniRoute's management API — keys, settings, backups, tunnels, MCP — and are served read-only via GET /api/agent-skills (no route-level auth; central MANAGEMENT classification applies). Collision: this corpus advertises the full management-plane control surface to arbitrary agents — a competing catalog to Carol's curated knowledge governance, publishing exactly the capabilities the HX lane keeps disabled.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — read-only, but it is a public advertisement of the entire control surface to any agent that can read it
capabilities.test_contract: GET /api/agent-skills and count entries vs the skills/ tree; content check: omni-mcp advertises 107 tools/32 scopes vs the measured scope list (17 MCP scopes — drift worth recording).
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Read-only catalog; removing the skills/ tree or the route removes the advertisement; nothing executes from these files server-side.

capabilities.name: Agent-skills SKILL.md generator (build tooling)
capabilities.purpose: generateAgentSkills rebuilds SKILL.md files from the OpenAPI spec and CLI registry with a hard safety contract — dryRun=true default, writes require dryRun=false, deletion requires prune AND dryRun=false (generator.ts:10-15) — and the generate route is management-gated. Collision: none material — doc synthesis tooling; its output feeds CAP-P7-025's advertisement concern.
capabilities.risk_class: low — filesystem writes possible only under explicit non-default flags
capabilities.test_contract: Run generator default (assert zero writes and a dry-run report); lab: dryRun=false against a temp copy and diff.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Default dry-run; generated files are overwritable artifacts (regeneration is the inverse).

capabilities.name: Plugin manager (install/activate lifecycle)
capabilities.purpose: The plugin manager coordinates scanner, loader, DB rows, and hook registry for install/activate/deactivate/uninstall, with assertWithinPluginDir (manager.ts:77-81) blocking rm of any path outside the plugin root even from a tampered DB pluginDir; the API tree is LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:56-57) as a child_process code-exec class. Collision: third-party code lifecycle inside the gateway — the plugin class is named in the charter's disabled-by-default list; nothing ships installed (scanner reads ~/.omniroute/plugins which is operator-populated).
capabilities.risk_class: high — third-party code lifecycle management inside the gateway process
capabilities.test_contract: Scan an empty plugin dir (zero plugins, no errors); lab: install a fixture plugin, activate, assert DB status transitions; negative: tampered pluginDir delete attempt throws.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Deactivate+uninstall via the API (path-guarded rm); LOCAL_ONLY tier blocks remote lifecycle calls; empty plugin dir means nothing loads at boot.

capabilities.name: Plugin loader (child-process isolation + env filtering)
capabilities.purpose: loadPlugin runs each plugin in a separate node child process over IPC (spawn process.execPath with a temp host script, stdio ignore/pipe/pipe/ipc, loader.ts:198-206) with a permission-filtered environment (getFilteredEnv allowlists safe keys unless the 'env' permission widens it, :386-395), SRI-format integrity hashing (:37-40), 10s hook timeout and SIGKILL grace. Collision: this is the gateway's third-party code execution engine — process-spawning class; the env filter is the only runtime permission enforcement found (see CAP-P7-903), so declared network/file/exec permissions are not code-enforced here.
capabilities.risk_class: critical — executes third-party code on the host; isolation is process-level only, permission enforcement partial
capabilities.test_contract: Load a fixture plugin and assert IPC ready/result round-trip; inspect the child env for allowlisted keys only; negative: hook timeout yields SIGTERM→SIGKILL cleanup.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Deactivate the plugin (child is killed, temp host script removed); no plugins loaded while none installed.

capabilities.name: Plugin manifest + permission schema
capabilities.purpose: plugin.json is validated against a manifest schema whose requires.permissions enum is network|file-read|file-write|env|exec (manifest.ts:11), defaulting to an empty permission list (:123), and the granted set is persisted to the DB at install/scan. Collision: the schema is the dashboard-visible contract for plugin authority — but enforcement beyond env filtering was not found (CAP-P7-903), so the declaration currently outruns the mechanism; owner review must treat manifests as claims, not guarantees.
capabilities.risk_class: medium — permission declarations without full runtime enforcement
capabilities.test_contract: Validate manifests missing/extra fields against the schema; assert DB row records the declared permission set at install.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Schema-level only; uninstalling plugins removes the rows.

capabilities.name: Plugin marketplace (remote registry install)
capabilities.purpose: The marketplace browses and installs plugins from a registry URL guarded by isSafeMarketplaceUrl — http(s) only, literal-private rejection, and A+AAAA DNS resolution with any-private-address rejection failing closed (marketplace.ts:35-60) — plus safeOutboundFetch public-only with redirect blocking for the fetch itself. Collision: remote code supply chain into the gateway (Phase 1 local seed registry, Phase 2 remote per the header) — the SSRF posture is strong, the supply-chain decision is the owner's.
capabilities.risk_class: critical — downloads and activates third-party code from a remote registry
capabilities.test_contract: Point at a lab registry fixture, install, assert integrity + manifest validation; negative: registry hostname resolving to a private IP is rejected (A and AAAA cases).
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Do not configure/use the marketplace (inert by default); installed plugins uninstall through the path-guarded manager.

capabilities.name: Plugin hooks + fs-watch hot reload
capabilities.purpose: Plugins register lifecycle hooks (onRequest/onResponse/onError/onInstall/onActivate/onDeactivate/onUninstall, manager.ts:31-40) that run in the request path, and a directory watcher auto-reloads changed plugin dirs after a 500ms debounce (watcher.ts:4,36-47). Collision: in-path request/response mutation by third-party code, plus filesystem-triggered code reload — a tampered plugin file becomes live code without any management action; the watcher means 'disabled by default' must include not watching empty dirs.
capabilities.risk_class: critical — unvetted code mutating traffic plus fs-triggered reload
capabilities.test_contract: Activate a fixture hook plugin and assert onRequest fires in order; touch a plugin file and observe debounced reload; negative: deactivated plugin emits no hooks.
capabilities.rollback_or_disable: Deactivation unregisters hooks (unregisterHooks) and stops watching; nothing watched while no plugins are installed.

capabilities.name: Pre-request middleware hooks (vm.Script compilation)
capabilities.purpose: The pre-request hook registry compiles operator-supplied JS into reusable vm.Script objects (registry.ts:111-118) that run in priority order BEFORE provider selection and can mutate body/headers, redirect to a different model/combo, or short-circuit a response (:7-13); the routeGuard classifies /api/middleware/ with the plugins code-exec tier and gates it LOCAL_ONLY (routeGuard.ts:58). Collision: arbitrary code rewriting routing decisions in the hot path — an ungoverned second routing brain competing with KK3's route governance; Coder-X independently classed it as untrusted-code-execution authority.
